card.text: Explore Dimorphos, the moon of Didymos, with its DART encounter shape.

introduction.text: Dimorphos is the small moon of Didymos that NASA’s DART spacecraft struck in September 2022. This view preserves its encounter-era shape, reconstructed from DRACO and LICIACube images. DART changed its orbit and shape; this surface is not a model of the altered asteroid.

shape.title: SPC shape model v004
shape.summary: Shape from DART and LICIACube encounter images, including modeled terrain. It is not a post-impact map.

draco.title: DART approach photographs
draco.summary: Four DRACO frames from 11 to 1.8 seconds before impact, using closer qualified detail where available. Brightness is approximately normalized; photographed shadows remain. Grid marks unobserved or rejected areas.

elevation.title: Shape-derived radial height
elevation.summary: Encounter-model height relative to a 75 m sphere. It shows the overall shape, not impact-induced changes.

albedo.title: SPC relative albedo model
albedo.summary: Grayscale shows modeled brightness before impact, not absolute albedo. Accepted facets cover about 31%; the grid marks the rest.

slope.title: Modeled surface slopes
slope.summary: Slope relative to modeled gravity, including uniform density, rotation and Didymos. This encounter-era model includes inferred terrain; it does not measure impact-driven change.
